synopsis: The corpus requires separate purposes, data and governance for failure discovery, performance estimation, and requirement/regression testing; coverage designs support understanding but must not supply the release-rate claim [f133, f6935, f11334, f14143]. Discovery deliberately concentrates on failures, so its failure fraction is not an operational rate; conversely, tuning against estimation cases can understate failures by turning the audit into a measure of fit to those cases [f6842, f14287, f14288]. Performance estimation uses a frozen, pre-registered, stratified random sample from the declared operating-domain distribution, with weighting and estimators fixed before inspecting results; correctly weighted rare-event campaigns require defensible distributions and known likelihood weights [f6939, f6941, f7288, f6951]. Search-found failures should become scenarios or regression tests, with their frequency estimated separately, while the estimation set is reserved for release candidates rather than continuous tuning [f6949, f6950, f13527]. The proposed release claim uses the frozen estimation sample plus physical anchors, and a four-month deadline makes stream separation a governance priority; the glossary's statement that a frozen random sample is the “only basis” needs qualification alongside the allowance for correctly weighted rare-event estimation [f7358, f14295, f14095, f7288].
